title: Prevention of insufficient home care of community-dwelling older adults
summary:
Due to the increasing aging of our society, the proportion of people in need of care will continue to rise in the coming years. Even now, the majority of these individuals are cared for at home by relatives. Since caregiving relatives are often already of advanced age themselves and face significant burdens in their caregiving role, they can suddenly become unavailable due to accidents, illness, or overload. The resulting acute care deficit at home not only poses a risk to those in need of care but also presents a challenge to society as a whole.

As part of the Prev-It project, a complex intervention is being developed to prevent care deficits in home settings. This consists, firstly, of a counseling intervention provided by care advisors and a Community Health Nurse to individuals classified within care levels one to three who are cared for exclusively by relatives. The aim of this counseling intervention is to enable care recipients and their relatives to proactively plan their future care situation and to build a support network to prevent care deficits.

Secondly, a needs assessment for an emergency care service will be conducted, which can be conceptualized in a follow-up project.

The counseling intervention is to be implemented in two model regions in the city and district of Rosenheim. Advisors will receive specific training for this purpose. Additionally, a coordination office for the prevention of care deficits is to be established, staffed by a Community Health Nurse. This nurse will train the care advisors already active in the model regions in the counseling intervention, carry out the intervention herself, and promote the development of networks focused on preventing care deficits at the community level.

The described complex intervention will be tested for feasibility and acceptance. Furthermore, in cooperation with the Integrated Emergency Dispatch Center Rosenheim, the Emergency Pastoral Care Rosenheim, pastoral workers from the Bavarian Red Cross (BRK) Rosenheim, and the Johanniter Rosenheim, a survey of acutely under-cared-for cases will be conducted. A systematic literature review on best-practice models for emergency care services will also be carried out.

The developed intervention aims to avoid unnecessary hospital admissions, thereby reducing burdens on individuals and costs for society. In addition, the intervention can help raise awareness in society as a whole about the risks of care deficits and the importance of timely prevention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At the individual level, we will include caregiving relatives and older adults in need of care (≥ 65 years) who are classified within care levels one to three. Caregiving relatives refers to all individuals who provide unpaid (excluding care allowance according to §37 SGB XI) and long-term physical care and/or household support and/or psychosocial assistance to a person in need of care from within their family or extended social circle.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for older adults in need of care:

•	Unable to provide written informed consent
•	Representation by a legal guardian
•	Insufficient proficiency in the German language, severe cognitive impairment as assessed by the care advisors/Community Health Nurse (a standardized cognitive assessment is not required, and re-assessment for inclusion is deemed inappropriate due to the burden on the individuals)

Exclusion criteria for caregiving relatives:

•	Unable to provide written informed consent
•	Insufficient proficiency in the German language
•	The care recipient, who is being cared for by the relative, refuses to participate in the study
